appraisal_events.evidence: For bowing at forty metres instead of joining the duke and the Queen of England: "J'aurais pu écrire un chef-d'œuvre, les Guermantes m'en eussent moins fait d'honneur que de ce salut"; the duchesse retails it to his mother, "que son mari avait été émerveillé de mon salut, qu'il était impossible d'y faire tenir plus de choses". The narrator reads the compliments as "encore moins une récompense pour le passé qu'une indication pour l'avenir", and the same aristocratic amiability that says "Mais vous êtes notre égal, sinon mieux" says it "pour être aimés, admirés, mais non pour être crus" — as Mme de Guermantes, once she saw his fears of not being invited were groundless and cost her nothing, declared them absurd and teased him at length.
appraisal_events.explanation: The Guermantes visibly honour him and the honour is real inside their world, but the narration shows it working as a lesson delivered to an inferior, calibrated never to dissolve the inferiority it soothes.

appraisal_events.evidence: Warned at the door — "Mais vous ignorez donc que le pauvre Mama est à l'article de la mort ? On vient de l'administrer" — he pushes past the bearer of the news: "Je le sais, je le sais... Le viatique a produit le meilleur effet", "ajouta-t-il en souriant de plaisir à la pensée de la redoute à laquelle il était décidé de ne pas manquer".
appraisal_events.explanation: The joke and the smile that frames it expose him: a dying man is worth exactly as much as the risk he might pose to the evening's programme.

appraisal_events.evidence: "ambitieux et timoré", vowed by diplomacy and the École des Sciences politiques "à la chasteté du chrétien", he has lost "la perspicacité spéciale qui se trouvait rarement en défaut chez M. de Charlus" and "n'arrivait même plus à reconnaître ceux qui, sous le déguisement de l'uniforme, étaient au fond ses pareils"; the names Charlus drops cause him "un étonnement délicieux", and while the whole young staff of the embassy comes to shake Charlus's hand he takes on "l'air émerveillé d'Élise".
appraisal_events.explanation: Vaugoubert is set beside Charlus as a blunted instrument — a man who no longer recognizes his own kind and must be told, marvelling, what everyone around him is.

status_effects.explanation: His standing rises visibly inside the world of the passage: the duke registers the bow among five hundred greetings, the duchesse reports it to his mother, and the family compliments him without cease.

The narration takes her amiability apart: the generosity offered once it costs nothing, the lie about not being known to have come home, the eyes lit for the evening and checked for their sparkle like the rest of the jewels.
He is convicted out of his own mouth of a callousness the passage does not soften.
He is diagnosed rather than described — timid, atrophied, decades behind what a trained ear hears at once.
The deference is staged and witnessed: an entire embassy staff files past to greet him and its whole young personnel comes to shake his hand, while the minister beside him marvels.

ambiguities: The passage's opening evaluative act — the Turkish ambassadress's rapture over the princesse de Guermantes and her demotion of the duchesse ("Oriane est une charmante femme du monde qui tire son esprit de Mémé et de Babal, tandis que Marie-Gilbert, c'est quelqu'un") — is left unrecorded because its speaker is a descriptor-identified figure outside the reference sheet's reviewed set; the narrator in any case voids the judgment by showing that it reversed the moment an invitation arrived, so neither Guermantes woman is credited with movement from it.
